Organization-level instructions can be missing from chat even when VS Code selects the expected organization. Existing trace output reports that the cache directory does not exist when instructions are read, but it does not show whether directory creation or the following file write succeeded.

This change adds trace logs before and after organization resource cache directory creation and cache file writes. If either filesystem operation fails, it logs the error with operation context and rethrows it so existing caller behavior remains unchanged.

No refresh, authentication, request, or cache behavior changes. Added focused tests for directory creation and file write failures.

title: Kimi: reduce tool calls / requests per turn (prompt-only, Kimi-gated)

labels.name: release-cherry-pick
labels.description: Automated cherry-pick between release and main branches

body:
## Why

`kimi-k2.7-code` has the highest requests-per-user-request and tool-calls-per-turn of all models (prod ~10 req / ~11 tool-calls per turn; median 2 but P90 34; ~11.5% of "heavy" turns drive ~63% of tool volume). Cost/turn and cache rate are already good — the problem is request **count** (and code survival). Requests are roughly equal to tool calls, so Kimi barely batches and every tool call is its own round-trip.

## Evidence (msbench run 29887843010, kimi-k2.7-code, vscbench, 144 inst, 46.5% resolved)

Steps: median 7, mean 16.7, p90 52, max 154 (failed median 9 vs resolved 6 — long heavy tail). Analysis of 11 extracted trajectories:

- **No parallelism**: tool-calls/request ~= 1.0 (one resolved outlier hit 1.98, proving Kimi *can* batch).
- **Redundant reads**: 98/265 read_file calls (37%) are exact duplicates; ~half re-read within <=3 calls; compaction was ~absent, so this is genuine redundancy, not context eviction.
- **Under-batched edits**: replace_string 71 vs multi_replace 17 (~4:1); 35 consecutive same-file single edits a single multi_replace would cover (worst case: 30 single edits, 0 multi).
- **Terminal thrashing** on the hardest/failed cases: `run_in_terminal` is the #1 tool (327 total); one failed instance did 101 terminal + 18 web-fetch calls in a debug spiral.
- `manage_todo_list` is broad but NOT a spam source (1–5 calls/inst) — ruled out.

Even the *resolved* heavy instance showed the same inefficiencies, so cutting them should reduce requests without costing success.

## Change (Kimi-only, prompt-only, in `kimiPrompts.tsx`)

- **A. Parallel reads/searches** — Kimi's read guidance was softer than the identical Anthropic/OpenAI wording; strengthened it to plan needed files/ranges up front and issue them as parallel reads in one message.
- **B. Anti-redundant-read** (top lever) — new guidance in `contextHandling` plus a concise per-turn reminder (`KimiReminderInstructions`): don't re-read a file/range already read; it stays available.
- **C. Edit batching** — made the multi_replace preference imperative: >1 edit => one `multi_replace_string_in_file` call.
- **D. Loop/terminal budget** — new `avoidingLoops` bullet: stop repeating edit-run-inspect cycles; form a root-cause hypothesis after a couple of failures.

## Deliberately NOT changed

- temperature/top_p (forced 1.0/0.95) — left untouched.
- No `parallel_tool_calls` request param (the API already permits parallel; it's a model-behavior gap).
- No structural compaction/context-window change (compaction was rare in the eval).
- No tool-surface removal (edit tools are already minimal for Kimi).

## Validation

- `tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.json` on the copilot extension: clean.
- `eslint kimiPrompts.tsx --max-warnings=0`: clean.
- Behavioral effect to be measured by benchmark eval on this PR.

## Follow-ups if the signal is weak

- Promote A/C into the per-turn reminder too; consider a Kimi-specific `read_file` nudge.

---
*Draft — opened for benchmark evaluation. Prompt-only, gated on `isKimiFamily`, so other models are unaffected.*

title: Webview view stuck after restart: persisted Service Worker state makes resource requests fall through to vscode-cdn.net ("Unable to preload CSS")
body:
<!-- Does this issue occur when all extensions are disabled?: N/A — reproducing requires an extension that contributes a webview view; the failure itself is in the platform webview resource-loading layer -->

- VS Code Version: 1.129.1 (8a7abeba6e03ea3af87bfbce9a1b7e48fed567b8) **and** 1.128.0-1783465401 (both affected; downgrading did not help)
- OS Version: Ubuntu 24.04.4 LTS, kernel 6.8.0-136-generic, x64 (X11 session)

## Summary

After a normal application restart that restores a window with a visible webview view, the webview's in-page resource requests are no longer served by the webview service worker. They fall through to the literal `https://file+.vscode-resource.vscode-cdn.net/...` host, every request fails, and the webview app dies during boot (stuck on its splash screen forever).

The state is fully deterministic on this machine:

- Delete `~/.config/Code/Service Worker` (+ `Code Cache`) → **next launch always works**.
- Any subsequent restart (session restore with the webview view visible) → **always broken**.

So a Service Worker registration persisted by the previous session appears to be the poison: the first launch after wiping SW storage registers fresh and works; every later launch reuses/collides with the persisted state and fails.

**Important scoping detail: not every webview in the window is affected.** The failure consistently hits the *heaviest* webview view (one that loads ~700 module chunks via `modulepreload`/dynamic import at boot), while a much lighter webview view from a different extension in the same windows keeps working every time. This looks like a race against service worker readiness/claim that only the webview with the largest earliest resource burst loses — not a total SW outage.

## Evidence captured inside the stuck webview

I prepended an error-capture shim to the affected extension's webview entry chunk (extension: `openai.chatgpt`, sidebar view `chatgpt.sidebarSecondaryView`). In the stuck state it recorded:

- 34 anonymous resource-load `error` events (capture phase, no message/filename — element load failures), then:

```
Uncaught Error: Unable to preload CSS for
https://file+.vscode-resource.vscode-cdn.net/home/erdun/.vscode/extensions/openai.chatgpt-26.5715.31925/webview/assets/app-main-BmDTPO5j.css
    at preload-helper-D1M5K2pS.js:1
```

- Heartbeat state while stuck: `{"ready":"complete","splash":true,"inflight":[]}` — document complete, app splash still shown, no in-flight fetches.

Meanwhile the renderer trace log for the same boot looks healthy from the outside:

```
[trace] Webview(8950b039-...): will update content
[trace] Webview(8950b039-...): webview ready
[trace] Webview.loadLocalResource - trying to load resource ... (≈700 entries, many "not modified")
```

i.e. the extension resolved the view and set HTML, `loadLocalResource` served resources, yet the page-side requests that go through the `vscode-cdn.net` route all fail.

## Additional observations

- Not extension-version specific: reproduced with two different versions of the extension.
- Not profile/state specific: reproduced after fully wiping `~/.config/Code` and `~/.vscode/extensions` (fresh profile breaks again from the 2nd launch on).
- Not VS Code-version specific: reproduced identically on 1.128.0 and 1.129.1.
- A second, much lighter webview view (different extension) in the same windows keeps working every time, so timing/size decides the outcome — consistent with a registration/claim race rather than total SW failure. The affected webview requests ~700 resources at boot (counted from `Webview.loadLocalResource` trace entries); the surviving one requests far fewer.
- Toggling the view closed/open after startup (i.e. re-resolving the webview later, once startup settles) usually recovers it — also consistent with a startup race.

## Workaround

Wrapping the launcher to delete `~/.config/Code/Service Worker` and `~/.config/Code/Code Cache` before every start makes every launch behave like a first launch and reliably fixes it.

## What I'd expect

Stale/persisted webview service worker state should never cause in-page resource requests to escape to the real `vscode-cdn.net` origin; the webview should wait for (or re-establish) a controlling service worker before the app's module graph starts loading.

title: Git: Avoid copying tracked files into worktrees
body:
Fixes #326935

cc @sandy081

When `git.worktreeIncludeFiles` contains a broad pattern such as `**/node_modules/**`, the Git extension walked matching ignored files up to partially tracked ancestors such as `build/` and `extensions/`. Recursively copying those directories could overwrite the freshly checked-out worktree with tracked files from the source checkout.

This change:

- enumerates ignored files and wholly ignored directories through Git;
- collapses only directories whose ignored contents all match;
- protects files tracked by the selected target ref, including cross-ref worktrees;
- preserves root, dotfile, Windows-separator, and trailing-separator glob behavior.

Regression coverage uses real temporary Git repositories to verify that dirty source files and source-ignored paths tracked by the target ref never modify the new worktree.

Tests:

- `npm run gulp compile-extension:git -- --quiet`
- `node node_modules/mocha/bin/mocha extensions/git/out/test/worktree.test.js --ui tdd --timeout 60000`
- `npm run precommit`

title: Agents window: chat response not rendered even though the data was returned (UI stops updating mid-stream; a window resize recovers it)
body:
## Summary

In the **Agents window**, a chat response sometimes **stops rendering part-way through even though the full response was actually returned**. The chat looks "stuck" — no more messages, no final answer, no follow-up — as if the model gave up. In reality **all the data has already been received by the client**; it just isn't painted to the screen.

**Resizing the window (e.g. shrink then maximize) makes the entire remaining response appear instantly.** This happens frequently — roughly **9 out of 10** long agent turns.

## Steps to reproduce

1. In the Agents window, start a long agent turn that streams a lot of content quickly (many rapid tool calls / a long streamed answer).
2. Watch the response render.
3. At some point it freezes mid-stream (often at a tool call) and never shows the final answer.

**Workaround:** resize the window — the full response (including the final answer) appears immediately.

## Actual behavior

- The response freezes at some point mid-stream, with blank space below.
- No final answer and no follow-up is shown, so it looks like the model hung / stopped processing.
- The input still shows the "working" / stop state.

## Expected behavior

- The response keeps rendering as it streams and the final answer is shown, without needing a manual window resize.

## This is **not** a backend / model / Agent Host problem

The model, SDK, Agent Host and AHP transport all deliver the **complete** response:

- The persisted SDK events (`events.jsonl`) contain the final assistant message and a clean turn end.
- The AHP wire log shows the full streamed content — **all `chat/delta`s for the final message** — followed by `chat/turnComplete`.
- No renderer exceptions are logged in `Window.log`.

So the data reaches the client and is stored in the chat view-model. The fact that a **resize reveals everything** confirms the content is already in the client and only needs a relayout to paint. **This is a client-side rendering/layout problem in the chat list.**

## Root cause (from live debugging with renderer logpoints)

I instrumented the renderer (CDP logpoints via `chrome-remote-interface`) across several streaming turns:

- **Auto-scroll itself is fine.** `ChatListWidget._withPersistedAutoScroll` runs correctly and follows the list's content height (its `scrollTop` tracks `scrollHeight`).
- **The virtualized list's content height stops keeping up with the stream.** The chat list is a virtualized tree whose `scrollHeight` grows only when the renderer reports per-row height changes:
  `ChatListItemRenderer.onDidChangeItemHeight` → `ChatListWidget._updateElementHeight` → `tree.updateElementHeight`.
  During rapid streaming these height events fire only **sporadically** (observed ~5–9 times in 3 minutes), while `refresh()` / `setChildren` runs 100+ times — and `setChildren` does **not** grow item heights. So the tree's `scrollHeight` lags the real DOM content.
- In one capture the tree's scroll model was **frozen** (`scrollTop=866, scrollHeight=1518` for ~90s while actively streaming), then jumped to the true height once the turn completed. Because auto-scroll pins to the (stale, too-short) content height, the newly-streamed content sits **below the tree's known range** and isn't shown until a relayout re-measures the rows.
- **No recovery affordance.** `_scrollLock` defaults to `true` and is set on submit for agent / auto-scroll turns, which **hides the scroll-down button** (`ChatListWidget.updateScrollDownButtonVisibility`: `atBottom = isScrolledToBottom || _scrollLock`). So even when the view stalls, there is no visible "jump to bottom" button. A window resize triggers `ChatWidget._layoutListForInputHeight` → `listWidget.layout()` → `tree.layout()` (a **full re-measure**) + `scrollToEnd()`, which is exactly why resizing recovers the content.

## Suspect code

- `src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/browser/widget/chatListRenderer.ts` — `fireItemHeightChange` (height-change emission, the "unchanged height" early-return, and the `_elementBeingRendered` suppression / initial-height scheduling).
- `src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/browser/widget/chatListWidget.ts` — `_updateElementHeight`, `_withPersistedAutoScroll`, `isScrolledToBottom`, and `_scrollLock` default (`true`) + `updateScrollDownButtonVisibility`.
- `src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/browser/widget/chatWidget.ts` — `setScrollLock(...)` on the accept-input path, and `_layoutListForInputHeight` (the resize recovery path).

## Notes / repro caveat

- Reproduces intermittently (~9/10 on long agent turns) and is **timing-dependent** (depends on streaming rate and how much the response row grows). In a clean dev build several turns rendered fine while one froze — consistent with a race in the height-reconciliation path.
- Easiest to reproduce with a long, actively-streaming agent turn that produces a lot of content quickly (e.g. many rapid tool calls with expanded output).

title: Chat: add an explicit agent-host model readiness signal (distinguish "still loading" from "authoritatively empty")
body:
## Summary

Model-restore / availability logic for **agent-host** chat sessions (Copilot CLI, Claude, Codex, remote agent hosts) currently cannot tell the difference between:

- **"still loading"** — the agent host has connected and registered its vendor, but hasn't published its model list yet (empty is **transient**), and
- **"authoritatively empty"** — the agent host has finished and genuinely has zero models (e.g. an unentitled/removed provider).

There is no explicit **agent-host readiness signal**. Today `hasResolvedVendor(vendor)` returns `true` as soon as *any* (even empty) model group is registered, so an empty list looks "resolved" before the real models arrive. This ambiguity forces every consumer to guess, and different consumers need opposite behavior for the same empty list.

## Why this matters (and what we did as a stop-gap in #326938 / follow-up)

The cold-start race where a restored/remembered agent-host model reset to **Auto** was fixed in #326938 by giving agent-host vendors the same "empty results are transient" grace that Copilot has — i.e. an absent model on an empty pool resolves as `pending` (wait) instead of `unavailable` (give up).

During review it became clear that this grace must **not** be applied uniformly, because an empty list is *sometimes* authoritative:

- **Restore resolution** wants leniency (wait for the pool during startup).
- **Cache-retention** (`mergeModelsWithCache`) and **send-availability** (`ChatInputPart.hasNoAvailableModel`, `sessionTypeAvailability`) want the empty list to be **authoritative** (evict stale cache, surface the "No models"/send-blocked state) — otherwise a removed/unentitled agent-host model can be offered from cache.

So we **scoped the grace to restore resolution only** (`resolveModelIdentifierFromCatalog`) and left cache-retention/availability treating a resolved-empty list as authoritative. That is the pragmatic separation, but it leaves a residue:

- For a **genuinely-empty** agent host, restore resolution now stays `pending` **indefinitely** (waits forever for a model that will never arrive). It's benign today (the send-blocked/`NoModels` UX is driven by live models + Auto support, not the restore wait), but it's not principled.

## Proposed: an explicit agent-host readiness signal

Introduce a first-class signal for _"this agent host has finished its initial model publication"_ (distinct from "a vendor group exists"). Then an empty list can be interpreted correctly everywhere:

- **not ready + empty** → transient → resolution waits, cache is retained to bridge the gap.
- **ready + empty** → authoritative → resolution concludes `unavailable`/defaults, cache is evicted, "No models"/send-blocked engages.

Sketch:
- Plumb a per-agent-host "models published / ready" state from the agent host connection through `ILanguageModelsService` (e.g. a `isVendorReady(vendor)` / `onDidChangeVendorReadiness` distinct from the current `hasResolvedVendor`).
- Feed it into:
  - `resolveModelIdentifierFromCatalog` (replace the `isAgentHostVendor` + empty-pool heuristic with the readiness signal),
  - `mergeModelsWithCache` (evict once ready-and-empty; retain while not-ready),
  - the restore waits in `ChatInputModelSelectionController` (stop waiting once ready-and-empty),
  - `hasNoAvailableModel` / `sessionTypeAvailability` for the send-blocked UX.
- Once in place, the special-case agent-host heuristics added in #326938 can be removed in favor of the readiness signal.

## Relationship to #326938 and the review comments

- PR: https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/pull/326938
- Review comment (separate resolution from cache-retention): https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/pull/326938#discussion_r3629236245
- Review comment (empty targeted pool is not necessarily still loading): https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/pull/326938#discussion_r3629236302

The reviewer explicitly suggested _"add an explicit agent-host readiness signal, or separate restore resolution from cache-retention policy, so the startup grace ends when an empty list is authoritative."_ #326938 does the **latter** (scoped separation); this issue tracks the **former** (the robust readiness-signal fix).

## Areas

- `src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/common/languageModels.ts` (`hasResolvedVendor`, `isAgentHostVendor`, `isLanguageModelVendorAbsenceConclusive`)
- `src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/common/modelSelection.ts` (`resolveModelIdentifierFromCatalog`)
- `src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/browser/widget/input/chatInputModelUtils.ts` (`mergeModelsWithCache`)
- `src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/browser/widget/input/chatInputModelSelectionController.ts` (restore waits)
- `src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/browser/widget/input/chatInputPart.ts` (`hasNoAvailableModel`) and `src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/browser/agentSessions/sessionTypeAvailability.ts`
- Agent host connection / `ILanguageModelsService` readiness plumbing

title: Chat: a fallback/automatic model (Auto) is persisted into session/draft input-state as if user-selected
body:
## Summary

An **automatically-selected fallback model** (e.g. `Auto`) is persisted into the chat session's input-state (and the empty-session draft memento) **as if it were the user's selection**. There is no gate distinguishing a user pick from a fallback/provisional selection when writing these stores.

This is a **separate concern from the "remembered pick" memento**, which is correctly gated and is being fixed on the restore side in #326938. Filing this so the persist-side principle — _"a fallback model should never be stored as though the user selected it"_ — can be addressed independently.

## The three model-persistence stores (and how they differ)

| # | Store | Key | Scope | Gated on user action? |
|---|-------|-----|-------|-----------------------|
| 1 | Remembered pick | `chat.currentLanguageModel.<location>[.<target>]` | PROFILE | ✅ **Yes** (`persistSelection = isUserAction && storeSelection`) |
| 2 | Session input-state | `chat.ChatSessionStore.index` (per session) | WORKSPACE | ❌ **No** (unconditional `setState`) |
| 3 | Empty-session draft | `chat.untitledInputState[.<tag>]` | WORKSPACE | ❌ **No** (unconditional) |

### Store 1 is correct
`ChatInputPart.setCurrentLanguageModel` only writes the remembered pick when the selection is user-initiated:

```ts
// src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/browser/widget/input/chatInputPart.ts
const persistSelection = isUserAction && storeSelection;   // fallback => false
...
if (persistSelection) { storeSelectedModel(...); }         // fallback => NOT written
```

Automatic selections use `applyModel(model, /*isUserAction*/ false, /*storeSelection*/ false)`, so `persistSelection === false` and the fallback is never recorded as the remembered pick.

### Stores 2 & 3 are not gated — this is the bug
`apply()` (even on the automatic path) still calls `_syncInputStateToModel()`, which writes the current model — **including a fallback `Auto`** — into the session state and the draft memento, with **no** user-action / selection-reason gate:

```ts
// src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/browser/widget/input/chatInputPart.ts
private _syncInputStateToModel(): void {
    ...
    const state = this.getCurrentInputState();          // selectedModel = current model (may be a fallback Auto)
    if (this._chatSessionIsEmpty) {
        this._emptyInputState.set(state, undefined);    // Store 3 — unconditional
    }
    this._inputModel?.setState(state);                  // Store 2 — unconditional (persisted by ChatSessionStore)
}
```

The infrastructure to distinguish a user pick from a fallback already exists but is **not consulted** here:
- `ChatInputModelSelectionController._provisionalModelId` (tracks a fallback that isn't the user's pick)
- `ChatModelSelectionModel.userExplicitlySelectedModel` / `selectionReason` (`FirstAvailable`, `ConfiguredDefault`, `SessionRestore`, `UserSelection`, ...)

## Evidence (current `main`)

Captured from a real profile (`user-data-dir`) after reproducing the agent-host cold-start race.

**Store 1 — remembered pick stays correct (the real user pick, not Auto):**
```
chat.currentLanguageModel.panel.agent-host-copilotcli = agent-host-copilotcli:gpt-5.6-sol
```
(No `.isDefault` marker is written on `main` — the write-side gate replaced it.)

**Store 2 — session input-state persisted the fallback Auto for sessions that hit the race:**
```
…/0c9444fc… -> copilot/auto                          ← fallback persisted as the session's model
…/c7222a35… -> agent-host-copilotcli:auto            ← fallback persisted
…/b674ecfd… -> agent-host-copilotcli:gpt-5.6-terra   ← real pick persisted (no race)
```

**Log cross-check** — the fallback is applied (not user-initiated, `persistSelection=false`), then immediately synced into the session state:
```
19:16:58.883 setCurrentLanguageModel to agent-host-copilotcli:auto … persistSelection=false
19:16:58.886 _syncInputStateToModel boundInputModelSession=…/untitled-c7222a35   ← unconditional write of Auto
```

## Impact

- Store 1 (remembered pick) is **not** affected — the user's explicit selection is preserved.
- Stores 2 & 3 carry a fallback `Auto` that was never chosen by the user. Today the user-visible harm is limited because `loadRemoteSession` prefers the request-history model over the stored draft, and #326938 makes the picker **wait** for the agent-host pool instead of applying `Auto` during the cold-start race (so `Auto` largely stops being applied → stops being persisted).
- However, the principle is still not enforced: **any** path that applies a fallback (e.g. a genuinely-removed model → `selectDefault`, or any race not covered by the waits) will still stamp the fallback into the session/draft state, unflagged — where it can later resurface / mask a remembered selection.

## Proposed direction (to discuss)

Enforce _"a fallback/provisional model is never persisted as though the user selected it."_ Options, increasing robustness:

1. **Read-side (cheapest):** on restore, always prefer a remembered/history model over a stored `provisional`/fallback draft model. (`loadRemoteSession` already does a version of this via #326938; extend it to the empty-draft path.)
2. **Write-side (cleanest):** gate the `selectedModel` written by `_syncInputStateToModel` on `!isProvisional` (using `_provisionalModelId` / `selectionReason !== FirstAvailable`), so a fallback isn't stored as the session's model — **or** store it but flag it non-authoritative (the modern equivalent of the old `.isDefault` marker) so restore ignores it in favour of a remembered/history model.

## Relationship to #326938

#326938 fixes the **restore/read** side of the cold-start race (agent-host vendors now get the same "empty results are transient" grace as Copilot, so a remembered/restored model waits for the pool instead of falling back to `Auto`). This issue tracks the **persist/write** side — ensuring a fallback that *does* get applied is never stored as a user selection. They are intentionally kept separate.

## Repro (to observe the fallback being persisted)

1. Open folder **A**; open a new chat editor for an agent-host session (Copilot CLI).
2. Select a specific model (e.g. **GPT-5.6**), send a message, wait for completion.
3. Fully exit VS Code.
4. Reopen VS Code in the same folder on a **cold start** (before the agent-host model list is cached) so the picker momentarily falls back to `Auto`.
5. Inspect `workspaceStorage/<id>/state.vscdb` → `chat.ChatSessionStore.index`: the affected session's `inputState.selectedModel` is stored as `…:auto`, even though the user never selected `Auto` (contrast with the PROFILE `chat.currentLanguageModel.*` key, which correctly retains the real pick).

### Areas
- `src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/browser/widget/input/chatInputPart.ts` (`_syncInputStateToModel`, `getCurrentInputState`, `setCurrentLanguageModel`)
- `src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/browser/widget/input/chatInputModelSelectionController.ts` (`_provisionalModelId`, selection reason)
- `src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/common/chatService/chatServiceImpl.ts` (`loadRemoteSession` read-side precedence)

Bug summary:

When running an interactive C++ console program using cppdbg with
"externalConsole": false, the pre-launch clang++ task completes successfully,
but the executable does not start in the integrated terminal.

The terminal displays "Build finished successfully," but the program's first
prompt never appears. VS Code then shows an active debug session even though
there is no running debuggee. Repeating the operation creates multiple stuck
debug sessions.

The same program works correctly when:

3. "externalConsole" is changed to true.

launch handoff on macOS.

#include <iostream>
using namespace std;

int main()
{
    int number = 0;

    cout << "Please enter a number: ";
    cin >> number;

}

{

}

3. Configure cppdbg:

    "program": "${fileDirname}/${fileBasenameNoExtension}",

    "externalConsole": false,

}

4. Open the C++ source file.
5. Select "Run C/C++ File" from the upper-right play button.
6. Wait for the build task to finish.

Expected result:

After the successful build, the executable should start in the VS Code
integrated terminal. The prompt should appear and accept keyboard input.

Actual result:

- The build finishes successfully.
- The integrated terminal continues showing only the build-task output.
- The program prompt never appears.

title: Restore last-used agent-host model instead of falling back to Auto
body:
## Summary

Agent-host chat sessions (e.g. **Copilot CLI**) publish their model list **asynchronously**, only after the agent host process connects. During that cold-start window, VS Code's model-restore logic treated a remembered/last-used model that wasn't in the (still-empty) pool as **conclusively unavailable** and reset the model picker to **Auto**, instead of waiting for the pool to load.

The result: after selecting a specific model (e.g. `GPT-5.6`) and reopening VS Code / a session / a different repo, the model picker showed **Auto** instead of the model you last used.

## Root cause

`isLanguageModelVendorAbsenceConclusive` only granted the built-in **Copilot** vendor a "an empty result during startup is transient" grace. Agent-host vendors (`agent-host-*` local, `remote-*` remote) load their models asynchronously too, but an empty resolution was treated as **final** → the remembered model resolved as `unavailable` → the restore gave up and fell back to Auto.

Because this defect is at the resolution layer, it leaked into **every** restore surface (a new editor, the sidebar chat view, and reopened existing sessions).

**Fix:** give agent-host vendors the same transient grace as Copilot, so an absent model on a still-empty pool resolves as `pending` (wait) rather than `unavailable` (give up):

```ts
return hasLiveModels || (hasResolved && vendor !== COPILOT_VENDOR_ID && !isAgentHostVendor(vendor));
```

This fixes all surfaces at once and naturally survives the transient empty resolutions emitted before the real models arrive (resolution stays `pending` until the pool loads). Two supporting hardening changes are included (see **Changes**).

## Issues fixed — with step-by-step repro

> These are agent-host sessions (Copilot CLI). The bug reproduces on a **cold start** — i.e. the first open before the agent-host model list has been fetched/cached. Reproducing reliably may require selecting a **non-Auto** model, sending a message, and fully **restarting** VS Code.

### Issue 1 — Reopening an existing session restores as Auto
1. Open folder **A** in VS Code.
2. Open a new chat editor for an agent-host session (Copilot CLI).
3. Select a specific model (e.g. **GPT-5.6**), send a message, and wait for completion.
4. **Fully exit** VS Code.
5. Start VS Code again in the **same** folder **A** — the previous session is restored automatically.
6. ❌ **Before:** the restored session's model shows **Auto**.
   ✅ **After:** the restored session shows the model you used (**GPT-5.6**).

### Issue 2 — Sidebar chat view opens on Auto after switching repos
1. Open folder **A**, select a model (e.g. **GPT-5.6**) in an agent-host session, send a message, wait for completion.
2. **Fully exit** VS Code.
3. Open VS Code in a **different** folder **B**.
4. Open a **new chat editor** — the model is correctly your last-used model.
5. Open the **Chat panel in the sidebar** (Copilot CLI).
6. ❌ **Before:** the sidebar chat shows **Auto** (even though the editor showed the right model).
   ✅ **After:** the sidebar chat shows your last-used model.

### Issue 3 — New chat editor in a different repo opens on Auto
1. Open folder **A**, select a model (e.g. **GPT-5.6 Terra**) in an agent-host session, send a message, wait for completion.
2. **Fully exit** VS Code.
3. Open VS Code in a **different** folder **B**.
4. Open a new chat editor for the agent-host session.
5. ❌ **Before (cold pool):** the model briefly/persistently shows **Auto**.
   ✅ **After:** the model shows your last-used model once the agent-host models load.

In all three cases the user's selection *was* saved correctly (in the per-session-type storage bucket); the bug was purely on the **restore/read** side — the picker gave up on the remembered model before the agent-host pool finished loading.

## Changes

- **`common/languageModels.ts`** — the root fix. Add `isAgentHostVendor(...)` (using platform-layer prefix helpers to avoid an import cycle) and exclude agent-host vendors from "conclusive absence", mirroring the existing Copilot behavior. This also lets `mergeModelsWithCache` keep cached agent-host models during the load window (same as Copilot).
- **`common/chatService/chatServiceImpl.ts`** — `loadRemoteSession` no longer drops the session's known model to `undefined` when the live lookup is cold; it carries the saved model (with metadata) into the restored input state, including through a transferred draft (new small helper `backfillRestoredModel`).
- **`browser/widget/input/chatInputModelSelectionController.ts`** — `syncFromConversationState` keeps waiting through transient empty agent-host resolutions and only falls back once the session-type pool has actually loaded without the model.

## Tests

New regression tests, **verified to fail if the root fix is reverted**:

- `modelSelection.test.ts` — `treats a resolved-but-empty agent-host vendor as still loading (pending)` (covers local + remote; and `unavailable` once the pool loads without the model).
- `chatModelSelectionModel.test.ts` — `initialize waits for a resolved-but-empty agent-host pool and restores the remembered model` (drives the restore through the real catalog resolver; asserts it waits through an intermediate empty event and applies the model on load) and `waits through a resolved-but-empty session pool and applies the restored model when it loads`.
- `chatService.test.ts` — `backfillRestoredModel` suite for the `loadRemoteSession` carry-over.

I temporarily reverted the root-fix clause and confirmed both new agent-host tests fail (`2 failing, 0 passing`), then restored it.

## Validation

- `npm run typecheck-client` ✅
- `npm run valid-layers-check` ✅ (new platform→chat import verified)
- ESLint on changed files ✅
- Suites: `ModelSelection` (55), `ChatModelSelectionModel` (19), `ChatInputModelUtils` (136, incl. cache — no regression), `backfillRestored`/`chatService` backfill (8) ✅

title: Make Add Selection to Next Find Match work with regex find mode
body:
Fixes #107090

## Problem

With regex mode enabled in the find widget, **Add Selection to Next Find Match** (`Ctrl+D`) does nothing. The reason: `MultiCursorSession` never receives the find widget's `isRegex` state — `findNextMatch` / `findPreviousMatch` / `findMatches` are always called with `isRegex = false`, so the regex pattern in the search box is searched literally and never matches.

## Fix

Thread the find widget's `isRegex` state through `MultiCursorSession`:

- When the find widget owns the search string (focus in the widget, widget revealed, search string non-empty), the session is created with `findState.isRegex` — mirroring how `Select All` already special-cases regex.
- When the selection owns the search text, behavior is unchanged (selected text is still matched literally).
- The session's `isRegex` is honored in `findNextMatch`, `findPreviousMatch`, and `findMatches`, so `Ctrl+D`, `Ctrl+K Ctrl+D`, and the previous-match variants all work with regex.

## Tests

Added a unit test (`issue #107090: AddSelectionToNextFindMatchAction works with regex find mode`) covering repeated `Ctrl+D` with a regex pattern. Ran the full multicursor suite: **18 passing**. `compile-src` finishes with 0 errors.

body:
## Feedback

> Also I know we made the decision to reduce the number of font weights being used (i.e. semibold font token is 600 instead of 500), but now that I'm seeing it in product this feels quite chunky (in a bad way).
>
> Thoughts on reverting this decision or making some specific exceptions?

**Source**: #ws-modernize-ui — Hawk Ticehurst on 2026-07-22

**Attachments**: [Screenshot 2026-07-21 at 8.01.13 PM.png](https://vscodeteam.slack.com/files/U0ALN6MH067/F0BK0T0MZ36/screenshot_2026-07-21_at_8.01.13___pm.png)

---

## Context

As part of the UI Modernization effort, the set of font weights was reduced and the semibold design token was standardized to a weight of `600` (up from `500`). Seeing this in product, the `600` semibold reads as too heavy/chunky across workbench surfaces, prompting a question about whether to revert the token to `500` or carve out specific exceptions.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Evaluate the semibold font token at `600` vs `500` weight in product across representative workbench surfaces (light, dark, and HC themes).
- [ ] Decide whether to revert the semibold token to `500`, keep `600`, or define specific per-surface exceptions, and document the rationale.
- [ ] Apply the agreed change to the font token(s) and verify the result matches the intended modernization visual language.
